chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn Isa, from 'Isa, from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
"O Zurarah, you begin the Adhan with four Takbirs, and conclude it with two Takbirs and two Tahliqs."
ai.seo_question: What is the prescribed number of Takbirs and Tahliqs in the Shia Adhan?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him), recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, establishes the specific numerical structure of the Adhan, prescribing four initial Takbirs and two concluding Takbirs with Tahliqs. This detail highlights the Shia emphasis on preserving the precise ritual form (Sunnah) of the call to prayer as transmitted through the Ahl al-Bayt, distinguishing it from other schools that may vary in the number of repetitions. It underscores the theological view that the Adhan is not merely a functional announcement but a structured act of worship with prescribed liturgical elements.
